issues: All 32 assigned records were read in full, including every retained body paragraph and the editorial summary/footnotes.
All cited quotations were checked as exact substrings of their cited packet paragraphs; paragraph locators use the packet's retained body-paragraph numbering.
Incoming Emma prose is never treated as Darwin voice. Emma's replies to Darwin are represented as reverse replies only.

DCP-LETT-448 has XML when=1838-11-30 although its body extends to Saturday 1 December; paragraphs 1–6 link to 444 and only paragraph 7 is linked to DCP-LETT-447. DCP-LETT-466, 481, and 484 are bounded multi-section records and their section dates constrain which incoming letters can be used.

DCP-LETT-466's Monday receipt establishes that two Emma letters were known by 31 December; the identifiable Gordon Square, linen/cook, and respirator responses occur in its Tuesday section and therefore establish topical known-by dates of 1 January. The two-letter acknowledgment does not prove one-to-one content allocation. Additional external letters may exist outside this pinned candidate set.

The preserved packet is a selected corpus, not an archive-wide absence proof. Exact external text needed for unresolved prompts includes the missing Darwin response to Emma 441 and the unassigned Darwin/Emma letters described in unlocated_references.
